last_observed_marker: October 20 local image 3 hardware test: directly observed HDMI and authenticated SSH, internal-Bluetooth DualSense pairing and input, a live stable-MAC Plasma Wi-Fi join with DHCP and HTTPS, and a full live Steam-to-Plasma-to-Gaming-Mode round trip with no compositor overlap; the Wi-Fi and session changes were not present in the original raw image
current_boundary: Run 15 remains the loader/display baseline; Runs 16-19 and 21 retain their historical scope. An exact unpublished local image 3 booted with HDMI and SSH, paired a wireless DualSense through the internal controller, and exposed gamepad, motion and touchpad input. Live follow-ups fixed the Plasma Wi-Fi menu with a stable permanent-MAC policy and fixed Steam Switch to Desktop by launching steam -steamos -gamepadui so Steam used its own legacy selector fallback. The final selector stopped graphical-session.target; both a remote return and the actual desktop shortcut returned cleanly to Gamescope/Steam without compositor overlap. A separate hosted image 3 draft completed successfully at 1d581df but is unbooted and predates those fixes. A replacement hosted artifact, offline-after-bootstrap behavior, Bluetooth cold-boot reconnect, a 60-minute Wi-Fi/Bluetooth soak, other consoles, video decode, integrity, bounded thermal stability, repeatability, and the minimal display subset remain uncharacterized.
notes: Linux booted with authenticated SSH in Runs 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 21; startup_64 and the preceding transition stages are inferred from authenticated userspace rather than direct instruction markers.
Run 15 PRE5/OP29 with the runtime clear disabled produced directly observed physical display output and authenticated Linux/SSH in the same cycle; it is the current hardware-verified baseline.
Run 16 reused the exact Run 15 loader and kernel with a distinct Ubuntu 24.04 initramfs, then produced directly observed physical output and authenticated wired SSH on the same console.
Run 16 is a cross-distribution control, not an independent hardware reproduction and not a reproduction of the exact Run 15 CachyOS initrd recipe.
Run 16 identified Marvell PCI 1b4b:2b56 and USB 1286:2059 wireless functions; the linked MT7921 driver cannot bind this hardware.

Run 17 loaded NXP mlan/moal built for the exact Run 16 kernel without the 7.2 compatibility patch and with objtool enabled; the driver downloaded the 11.60 p47 firmware, scanned both bands, joined a 5 GHz network, and carried an HTTPS download over Wi-Fi.
Run 17 needed a second wake attempt; after the first, the console stayed pulsing blue with no network, and the cause was not isolated.

Run 18 booted CachyOS with an opt-in 11.60 loader build that carries upstream's 13.60 low-memory reservation (upstream 8cda4c1). It differs from the Run 15 ELF only in the three E820 operands in the inner HV, the wake blob that carries it, and the outer build id.
In Run 18 the e820 map passed to Linux showed 0x100000-0xffffff as System RAM and 0x1000000-0x3fffffff as device reserved, as intended; MemTotal was 14,783,608 kB.

Run 18 wrote three 4 GiB files to the USB root, dropped caches, and re-read them with matching SHA-256 and no new kernel errors. The Run 15 loader was not put through the same check and the read/write errors reported by testers were never reproduced on this console, so Run 18 does not show that the reservation fixes them.
Run 18 DRM state reported card0-DP-1 connected at 1920x1080 and a KDE Plasma session started, but the picture was not recorded as directly observed.

Run 19 booted the image and ELF from the tester guide: CI Ubuntu 24.04 image release ubuntu2404-1160-build-3 and the DMA E820 loader ELF from release firmware-11.60-dma-e820-run18. It is the first recorded hardware boot of that pair and of a CI-built image on this console.
In Run 19 the operator directly observed the HDMI picture. The loader output was byte-identical to Run 18, and the e820 table and MemTotal matched Run 18.

Run 19 ran the tester guide checks as written, including the optional 3 x 4 GiB write and read-back check, which passed with no storage error lines. It used the same console and USB drive as Run 18 and had no A/B control, so it does not show that the reservation fixes the tester errors.

Run 19 found two image defects for the backlog: the hostname is the CI build container ID, and ps5-ssh-host-keys.service causes an ordering cycle with ssh.socket that systemd breaks by dropping the sockets.target job. SSH still worked.

The dma_e820_build record describes Run 18 only; its physical_display_observed and ubuntu_ci_image_tested values are Run 18 results. Run 19 (ubuntu_ci_dma_run) booted the DMA build with the CI Ubuntu image and a directly observed picture.

Run 21 is the first boot of Linux 7.3.0 and of the bounded Wi-Fi loader on this console. The kernel is mainline v7.3 with the 7.3 port of the PS5 patches by rmux (Armandas Kvietkus), https://github.com/rmuxnet/ps5-linux-patches-1 at 36f173f, which also brings rmux's PS5 CPU and GPU frequency drivers. The planned Runs 21 (CachyOS 7.3) and 22 (Wi-Fi) were merged into this run, and Run 20 was deferred.

Run 21 booted a local build of the cachyos-1160-k73 image branch from before the review fixes, not a CI build. CI build cachyos1160-k73-image-1 completed successfully afterwards and is held in a draft release; it has not been booted and is superseded by image 2.

CachyOS image 2 is source-pinned by tag cachyos1160-k73-image-2 at 346088a48f66eb956dafdec9de5085e73b2d44a5. It uses rmux's 36f173f Linux 7.3 patch as published, then applies a separate hash-pinned IW620 Bluetooth quirk-ordering follow-up; it also puts the firmware copy before the explicit Wi-Fi driver load, packages linux-ps5 7.3.0-2 with KBUILD_BUILD_VERSION=2, keeps the frequency drivers manual, and enables ps5fan.service with fixed maximum servo pattern 3 rather than a dynamic temperature curve. Workflow 39481460775 completed successfully. Its public tester prerelease contains one 1,943,471,712-byte ps5-cachyos1160-k73.img.xz with SHA-256 8b785243f79a32a4155cc1e39bed01d580e25ca514e88abbfed1a8a8157a281a; it expands to the 12,582,912,000-byte raw image with SHA-256 3798c7dba96412c5301eb201d8bf8aa4edd1b2f80a743dfd7b90b2a79222c62d. Those are verified build and release facts, not hardware results, and image 2 has not been booted.

Steam's Switch to Desktop and joining Wi-Fi from the KDE menu remain unresolved after the image 2 source changes. Releases use one .img.xz and fail instead of publishing numbered parts if the compressed image reaches 2 GiB.

An exact local image 3 from source f7d6fbd booted with directly observed HDMI and authenticated SSH. Its raw SHA-256 is 5a904e02f6a2908be91054b7b73ebf6f891fece0edc1a88f2f9d60264d7556d4; it is not published and is not the hosted draft.

On the local image 3, the internal Bluetooth controller registered and a wireless DualSense paired, bonded, trusted and connected. Buttons, motion sensors and touchpad input worked with no USB DualSense present. One short concurrent Wi-Fi/Bluetooth check passed; cold-boot reconnect and soak remain pending.

The local image 3 initially reproduced the Plasma Wi-Fi access-point-not-in-scan-list failure. Disabling NetworkManager scan MAC randomization, retaining the IW620 permanent address and keeping wifi.powersave=2 made the normal Plasma menu pass WPA3 association, DHCP and HTTPS. This was a live change, not a property of the original raw image.

The original image 3 desktop listener received no matching system-bus call. Manual selector plus tty1 getty restart opened Plasma. Relaunching as steam -steamos -gamepadui made Steam intentionally use its legacy selector fallback; sudo /usr/bin/steamos-session-select plasma was observed, Gamescope exited and Plasma/KWin started.

A later remote selector invocation stopped the owning user graphical-session.target in 0.086 seconds. KDE exited and Gamescope/Steam started with no overlapping compositor. Current source uses only that target stop and no later process kill or login-session termination. The actual desktop shortcut also passed with the final 3,736-byte selector (SHA-256 1d099eeacc19bbf575e5a636fc81087a46f72af64390172e437372b493bde1c1): the token changed at 5.709 seconds and 0.563 seconds later Gamescope was running with no KWin or Plasma shell. The exact replacement artifact still has to reproduce the round trip.

Hosted workflow 39510517216 succeeded at 1d581df. Its 1,943,469,912-byte archive SHA-256 is 8cdbe317334ec8f2a53adad7c59d580ddf5711cdda03c15b642de6347fa8a1a9 and its 12,582,912,000-byte raw SHA-256 is 82088537470f698b01aa198319b205d347de928fbe3acd3c7a49a9a8acf0e314. The draft is unbooted and predates the stable-MAC, Plasma-first, -steamos launcher and return-selector changes, so it must be replaced before publication.

The Run 21 loader (firmware-11.60-dma-e820 at 98925a2, target linux-1160-dma-e820-bounded-wifi) checks the boot files against bounds instead of exact sizes, prints its refusals, and dumps the 11.60 IW620 firmware. The Run 15 and Run 18 loaders refuse these boot files. In Run 21 it dumped the 498,108-byte firmware for the first time on 11.60, and the wake copy stayed inside the proven window.
In Run 21 the e820 table matched Runs 18 and 19, and KASLR put the kernel code at physical 0x26ec00000, far above the reserved range. MemTotal was 14,788,356 kB.

In Run 21 the Wi-Fi driver first probed before the firmware was in place, then the image's firmware service reloaded it and the 17.130.3.p47 firmware came up. Joining from the KDE menu failed twice; joining by name with nmcli worked, on 5 GHz with WPA3, and a 50 MB HTTPS download over Wi-Fi ran at about 192 Mbit/s.
In Run 21 Bluetooth did not work: btusb bound 1286:2059 but no controller came up. A DualSense over a USB cable worked. VCN initialized with its firmware, but video decode was not tried.

In Run 21 rmux's GPU frequency driver, loaded by hand, brought idle temperature from about 50 C to about 36 C with the GPU at 400 MHz and a normal picture; the CPU driver added at most about 0.5 C at idle. The drivers are not autoloaded in this image.

After the initial Run 21 checks, Steam completed a 53,229,366,208-byte download and committed 347 files. A watcher took 480 snapshots over about four hours; free space moved from 213G to 159G and every snapshot had zero new matching storage-error lines relative to the watcher's baseline. The watcher's diskstats throughput and total counters are invalid because it read I/O-time fields 7 and 11 instead of sector fields 6 and 10. This was not a read-back, hash, or operator-run Steam integrity pass.

Run 21 later recorded 540 five-second game-load samples: GameThread appeared in 88, the GPU was at 2.23 GHz in 76, the transition table recorded 386,159 ms at 2.23 GHz, and temperature peaked at 84.0 C. The logger ended while load remained active without operator-confirmed gameplay or display, so this is not a thermal-equilibrium or stability result. The frequency drivers remain manual-only.
The ubuntu_wifi record describes Run 17; its loader_dump_hardware_tested value is a Run 17 result. Run 21 (cachyos_k73_run) is the first run in which the loader dumped the Wi-Fi firmware.

Run 15 remains the release loader baseline; the DMA E820 build is a separate opt-in build. Run 18 remains the DMA validation run, Run 19 the Ubuntu tester-pair run, and Run 21 the first CachyOS 7.3.0 boot with the bounded Wi-Fi loader.
Run 14 PRE3/OP0 with the runtime clear disabled remains the initializer-only control.
The exact Run 13 PRE3/OP0 ELF failed twice and must not be described as working.

The attached physical USB FAT boot partition passed verification and its active files exactly match the Run 12 hashes, which Runs 14 and 15 also used; the Linux root partition was not directly mounted on macOS.

Before Run 15, AMDGPU, EDID, connector state, and a direct modeset succeeded in Linux without physical output. Run 15 shows that the complete added pre-Linux sequence and configuration were sufficient in the successful cycle; it does not isolate the necessary component.
The historical split post-wake userland flow stopped responding and remains retired.
The pLinux-derived wake-coupled candidate is superseded.
The clean official-loader Stage 0 and reversible Stage 1A alias transaction both passed on hardware with a responsive UI.
Stage 1B passed a 16 KiB data read-through canary through the exact mirrored syscore subtree, entered its mandatory cold-reboot hold, and left the GameOS UI responsive.

Stage 2A published the exact 240-byte inert wake blob RX at 0xffff800000000000 in the PID-1 pmap, verified the full source bytes and page permissions, and entered its mandatory backing hold without a hook, HV write, rest mode, or Linux action.
GameOS remained responsive during the Stage 2A backing hold; cleanup requires a cold reboot.
Stage 2B-3 passed the exact startup_mp S3 resume boundary and complete carrier restoration without executing the alias.
Stage 2B-4 isolated a wake-time hang to the new direct RET into the PID-1-only alias; the console remained continuously pulsing blue and emitted no PASS marker.
The later Sonic-style copy-to-kernel-text carrier reached authenticated Linux and supersedes the failed direct-alias transfer.
Run 14 retained the direct 11.60 mp3_initialize(0) call, disabled only the redundant clear, and reached authenticated Linux; the initializer is validated in this wake context.
Within the controlled Run 12/13/14 sequence, the Run 13 regression is isolated to the redundant 10,252-byte alias clear; exact-11.60 production must omit it to match Sonic.

Run 15 added MP3 commands 21 and 22, all 29 display-table records, Sonic's response-first buffer layout, and the outer-call/leaf-tail-jump dispatcher; without UART, individual return values were not observed.
Run 15 is one successful full-path cycle; repeatability, monitor coverage, and the minimal necessary subset of the 29 operations are not yet characterized.
